content.content:
# Mine

Mine is a set of PWAs (Progressive Web Apps) to digitalize ones personal or professional life.
The key idea is to save everything in a repo as markdown files. This can be calendar entries,
diaries, markdowns extracted from voice recordings / pdfs / .. These .md files can easily be
ported to new apps without a vendor lock-in and are processed via an (AI) assistant to help you
plan your day, keep track of tasks, remind you of memories a.k.a. a second brain.

To keep complexity to a minimum each use-case lives in a separate folder. e.g. the calendar PWA
lives completely in a 'calendar' folder as does the zettelkasten and all the other apps. Each
folder contains a 'sample' folder with samples how the markdowns shall look, a REQUIREMENTS.md
describing how the PWA works and a TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md describing how it is built.

See [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) for how this is built, and
[TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md](TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md) for how it is checked.

## One app, one setup

Mine installs as **one** app on the phone, with one icon. The apps in the subfolders are pages
inside it, not separate installs.

This is what makes the central requirement work: **the GitHub repo and token are entered once,
in the main app, and every app in a subfolder uses them.** Verified on iPhone and Android.

## Main app

A tile per app: its `icon.svg` above its folder name.

Above the tiles, apps may contribute a summary. The calendar's shows today's entries and the
next one — which matters, because opening the app is the only reminder that works (see below).

## First run

1. Open the app URL and add it to the home screen (iOS: Share → Add to Home Screen;
   Android: menu → Install).
2. The setup screen asks for GitHub owner, data repo, branch, and a personal access token.
3. The app tests the connection and reports clearly if it fails.

Settings are stored on the device only. The token is never displayed again after entry, and the
app warns 14 days before it expires.

Two settings belong to Mine rather than to any one app, and the same two rows appear in the main
settings and in each app's: **theme** (system, light or dark) and **date format** (auto, which
follows the device's locale, or `dd.mm.yyyy`, or `mm/dd/yy`). Both default to following the
device, so Mine looks like the rest of the phone until you say otherwise.

One convention is the same in every app: **a save icon is green and a trashcan is red**, wherever
either appears — a trashcan is red even where it only clears one field of a form that has not
been saved, because the rule is the icon, not the consequence. Both are **glyphs on no
background**: a save is a green disk, a trashcan is a red trashcan. **Nothing in Mine is a filled
green button.** The weight of a primary action comes from the icon being the familiar one in the
familiar corner, not from a block of colour — and a save drawn like the rest of the row cannot be
mistaken for a background that means something. The `x` that closes or abandons something is
neither green nor red, and stays plain.

## Using it

- Changes appear instantly and are queued for GitHub in the background.
- A sync indicator shows: in sync / pending / error.
- Offline, the queue is kept and sent when you are back online or reopen the app.
- Editing the same entry on two devices never loses either version: the other device's version
  keeps the file, yours is kept beside it and flagged, and the sync indicator tells you there is
  something to review. Nothing is discarded and nothing is silently overwritten — but the app
  does not interrupt you to ask which to keep, because by then you are somewhere else.
- Everything works offline, including dates and search, because the app keeps a full local copy.

## Reminders

**Mine cannot notify you while it is closed.** No browser can schedule a notification for later;
this is a platform limitation, not a missing feature. Alerts are stored with each entry and
exported, and they fire while the app is open. The summary on the tile screen is the reminder.

## Updates

When a new version is deployed the app shows "Update ready — reload". It never updates while you
are in the middle of editing.

The banner appears only when the version waiting to take over genuinely differs from the one
running. A new worker can sit waiting while being identical to the active one, so "a worker is
waiting" is not the test — if it were, the banner would appear on an app with no update at all
and never go away. Reloading twice with no deploy in between must leave no banner.

## Privacy

Your data lives in a **private** repo. The app itself is public, but it contains no data, and the
token is scoped so that it can only touch the data repo.

content.content:
1	# Calendar
     2	
     3	Calendar is an app of [Mine](../REQUIREMENTS.md) to manage your calendar. Every entry is one
     4	markdown file in the data repo, so your calendar stays readable and portable without this app.
     5	
     6	See [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) for the file format.
     7	
     8	## What an entry holds
     9	
    10	A title, a type — **event** or **task** — a start and end, a group, a location, participants,
    11	alerts, and a free markdown body for the agenda, checklist or notes.
    12	
    13	A task also carries a **stage** — `todo`, `doing` or `done` — and, optionally, a priority (1, 2
    14	or 3) and an estimate in days. An event has none of the three. Stage is the only record of a
    15	task's progress; there is no separate done flag.
    16	
    17	A new task starts at `todo` with an estimate of **1 day**. Both are only defaults: either can be
    18	changed before saving, and the estimate can be cleared away again, so `estimate` stays a key an
    19	entry may simply not have — nothing writes one into a task that never carried one.
    20	
    21	Entries can repeat, and a repeating entry can have single occurrences skipped, moved, retitled
    22	or moved to another stage without affecting the rest.
    23	
    24	## Layout
    25	
    26	A navigation pane at the top and a big calendar window below it.
    27	
    28	In the top pane, three groups: the two view controls at the left, the period in the middle, the
    29	two ways out at the right.
    30	
    31	```
    32	[board]    [filter]     [‹] [NOV/26 ▾] [›]     [⚙] [⌂]     a calendar view
    33	[calendar] [filter]     [‹] [7 ▾]      [›]     [⚙] [⌂]     the kanban
    34	[board]    [filter]       [NOV/26 ▾]           [⚙] [⌂]     either one, on a phone
    35	```
    36	
    37	Everything in the pane is drawn at **twice the size** it was: this is the row reached for on
    38	every visit, and it was the smallest thing on the screen. On a phone the controls **share the
    39	row width equally and the pane stays on one line**, down to a 320 px viewport — it neither wraps
    40	onto a second line nor drops a control, because five controls spread across the full width is
    41	exactly what fits at this size.
    42	
    43	- **Leftmost, the view switch and the filter.** One slot always holds the way to the other kind
    44	  of view: a board icon in a calendar view, and on the board a calendar icon, which returns to
    45	  the month view. The board is not a zoom step, which is why it has a slot of its own rather
    46	  than a place in the cycle the label walks. Beside it a dropdown to filter by group, each group
    47	  showing its colour. This is a
    48	  view filter and is remembered per device; groups are *named and coloured* in settings, not
    49	  here.
    50	- **Centred, the period.** Left/right buttons, with the period label between them, to move to
    51	  the previous/next day, week, month, year or sprint, depending on the current view. The label
    52	  is short, because the pane has to fit a phone:
    53	
    54	  | view | label |
    55	  | --- | --- |
    56	  | day | `FR 20/NOV` |
    57	  | week | `W47/NOV` |
    58	  | month | `NOV/26` |
    59	  | year | `2026` |
    60	  | kanban | `7` — the sprint number alone |
    61	
    62	  The month name is the device locale's three-letter abbreviation, upper-cased, so a German
    63	  phone reads `OKT/26`: short beats English. The week label always carries its ISO week number,
    64	  whether or not *show calendar weeks* is on — that setting governs the month view's gutter and
    65	  nothing else. A week spanning two months takes the month its **fourth** day is in, which is
    66	  the rule the gutter already uses, so label and gutter can never disagree.
    67	
    68	  **Clicking the label zooms the calendar**: year → month → week → day → year, and round again.
    69	  It is a cycle rather than a scale with two ends, because a single target cannot be disabled at
    70	  an end and still be the way on. So there is no `-` and no `+` in the pane, and no
    71	  `D` `W` `M` `Y` `K` row either. On the board the label is the sprint number and clicking it
    72	  opens the list of sprints instead; the board has no zoom.
    73	
    74	  **The caret `▾` beside the label is a button of its own** and opens the dropdown picker. It
    75	  has to be, now that the label itself zooms — the picker is the only way back to today, so it
    76	  cannot be a tap that the zoom has taken. The dropdown shows a month at a time, with its name
    77	  top left and left/right arrows top right. Clicking the month name switches to a year grid of 9
    78	  years ending with the current one, whose arrows page by 9 years. Today is highlighted in it,
    79	  and tapping it is how you get back to today — there is no jump-to-today button in the pane. In
    80	  the kanban the dropdown picks a sprint, and there the caret and the label do the same thing,
    81	  since that list is the picker: its rows read `Sprint 7 · 19 Jan – 1 Feb`, and the row holding
    82	  today reads `current · 19 Jan – 1 Feb` on a brighter background in dark mode, a darker one in
    83	  light.
    84	
    85	  **On a phone there are no `‹` `›`.** The label is swiped instead: a swipe left steps forward, a
    86	  swipe right back — through periods in a calendar view, through sprints on the board. **The
    87	  swipe lives on the label alone.** Nowhere else in the app does a sideways gesture do anything,
    88	  so it never has to be told apart from a card drag on the board or from a scroll in a grid.
    89	- **Rightmost, the two ways out.** A gear button that opens settings, and a home icon back to the
    90	  Mine tile screen. A house rather than an arrow, because a third arrow beside the two that step
    91	  through periods reads as another way to move inside the calendar.
    92	
    93	All views show **seven columns beginning with the configured first day of the week**, with
    94	Saturday and Sunday tinted wherever they land. A Saturday task has to be visible.
    95	
    96	When *show calendar weeks* is on, each week row carries its ISO 8601 week number in a left
    97	gutter, separated from the days by a thin vertical rule. The number is always ISO, whichever
    98	day the week is set to start on. ISO weeks run Monday to Sunday, so a row beginning on Sunday
    99	holds one day of one ISO week and six of the next; the number shown is the one the rest of the
   100	row is in.
   101	
   102	**There is no `+` in the top pane.** An entry is created where it will live: by clicking empty
   103	space in a day, week or month cell, by the small `+` in the day preview, or — in the kanban — by

   110	  is highlighted. A day with entries takes the background colour of its group, split between
   111	  colours if there are several — a year grid has no room for anything else. Clicking a day shows
   112	  that day's entries, as a preview like everywhere else. **The month's name is a button**: it
   113	  reads as a caption but is pressable, with a hover and a press state, and clicking it zooms

   127	  cell's edge with no `…`**, because three dots cost three characters in the one place in the app

   129	  carries **no done-rectangle** — that width goes to the title; one-tap done stays in the week

   131	  or on the board. Clicking empty space in a cell creates an entry; clicking an entry opens it.
   132	- **Week** — columns are the days, rows are the 24 hours.
   133	- **Day** — the week view for a single day, with more detail per entry.
   134	- **Kanban** — below.
   135	
   136	Groups switched off in the filter are not shown in any view.

   138	### The day preview
   139	
   140	Clicking a day opens that day's entries as a list, each one tappable. Its top right carries a
   141	small `+` to add an entry on that day and a small `x` to close it — not full-width buttons. It
   142	is reached from a day in the year grid, from a day cell in the month view on a phone, and from
   143	a day header in the week and day grids.
   144	
   145	## Entry popup
   146	
   147	The popup **opens in the middle of the screen**, on a phone as much as on a desktop — and so
   148	does every other overlay in the calendar: a field's own popup, the settings panel and the day
   149	preview. Nothing rises from the bottom edge any more. A centred card is reached with either
   150	thumb and does not pretend to be a drawer that can be dragged.
   151	
   152	A row of icon buttons at the top, and it now holds the type pair and the three on the right and
   153	nothing between them. **Every button in it is an icon; no button carries a letter.**
   154	
   155	- Leftmost, a ticked square for **task** and a calendar page for **event**. Choosing one
   156	  deselects the other; the default is event. What the entry *is* comes first, because it governs
   157	  what the rest of the popup offers.
   158	- Then, right-aligned: an `x` to close and discard, a trashcan to delete the entry, and a disk
   159	  to save it.
   160	
   161	There is no dash between the two groups: the gap to the right-aligned trio already separates
   162	them, and the field icons the dash used to divide off are not in this row at all any more.
   163	
   164	Below it, in this order: the **title**, the **start and end** fields, the **toggle row**, and
   165	then **one row per field**.
   166	
   167	### The toggle row
   168	
   169	One row of icons directly under start and end. These are not fields with a form each: they are
   170	small values, edited in the row itself, and they **show their value** rather than merely whether
   171	they have one — each as a small badge on the corner of its icon.
   172	
   173	- a sun for **all-day**. **A clickable icon, not a checkbox** — lit when on, plain when off, the
   174	  one icon in the popup that still lights, because it is the one with no value to show. On an
   175	  event it is alone on the row.
   176	- three small columns for **stage** — cycles `todo` → `doing` → `done` on each tap, its badge in
   177	  that stage's kanban colour: red, yellow, green. There is no stage popup.
   178	- a flag for **priority** — cycles none → 1 → 2 → 3 → none, the badge carrying the digit on that
   179	  priority's chip colour.
   180	- an hourglass for **estimate** — the one that opens a popup, because a number has to be typed.
   181	  Its badge reads the day count as `2d`, exactly as a kanban card shows it. It stays on this row
   182	  rather than joining the field rows below, because what it carries is a badge-sized value like
   183	  the other three, not a form.
   184	
   185	On an event, stage, priority and estimate are not there at all, because an event has none of
   186	them. They sit here so that a task that is not on a board still carries the two fields a kanban
   187	card edits.
   188	
   189	All-day is deliberately **not** the save button's green: in all of Mine green is a save and red
   190	is a trashcan, and a green toggle beside the disk would make the popup look like it offers two
   191	primary actions.
   192	
   193	### The field rows
   194	
   195	Every other field is a row, and **every field has a row, set or not** — the rows are now the only
   196	way to reach a field, so none of them can be hidden. A row is the icon on the left and the
   197	field's name beside it, and, when the field is set, its value after that:
   198	
   199	```
   200	[ball]    Category     Work
   201	[pin]     Location     Conference room 3B
   202	[lines]   Details
   203	[repeat]  Repeat
   204	```
   205	
   206	The six fields, in their canonical order:
   207	
   208	- three lines of text for **details** — the markdown body;
   209	- a ball for **category**;
   210	- circular arrows for **repetition**;
   211	- a bell for **alerts**;
   212	- a pin for **location**;
   213	- a person for **participants**.
   214	
   215	- **Clicking a row opens that field's popup.** The row *is* the pen, so no row carries one, and
   216	  clearing a field is the trashcan inside its popup, which is already there.
   217	- **The rows that are set move to the top.** Set fields come first, unset ones follow, and inside
   218	  each group the order is always the canonical one above. Setting a field lifts its row into the
   219	  top group and shuffles nothing else, so a row never moves for a reason you did not cause.
   220	- **A set row is plain.** Being in the top group and showing a value is what says the field is
   221	  set — which is what the old lit icon said, in a row that no longer exists. Nothing in the
   222	  popup lights except the sun.
   223	
   224	Each of the six opens its own popup, and every popup has the same three buttons: a trashcan that
   225	clears that one field, an `x` that abandons the sub-edit, and a disk that commits the value into
   226	the entry form. **A sub-popup never writes to the repo**, with the single exception noted under
   227	Category.
   228	Nothing is written until the entry popup's own disk, so one entry edit is one commit, and the
   229	entry popup's `x` discards the staged fields along with everything else. This is also what makes
   230	a brand-new entry work, since it has no file for a sub-popup to write to.
   231	
   232	Saving **closes the popup and returns to the calendar immediately**; the push to GitHub runs in
   233	the background and is reported in the sync line, not in the popup.
   234	
   235	### Repetition
   236	
   237	A dropdown, not an RRULE field:
   238	
   239	```
   240	does not repeat · daily · weekly · every 2 weeks ·
   241	monthly on the x-th · monthly on the x-th weekday · yearly
   242	```
   243	
   244	below it an **ends** control: never, on a date, or after a number of occurrences.
   245	
   246	Files may be hand-written or imported, so a rule the dropdown cannot express — `the last Friday
   247	of the month`, `Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays` — is shown as a non-selectable **custom** state
   248	displaying the rule as text, with a note that choosing an option will replace it. Saving the
   249	entry without touching the dropdown leaves the rule untouched. No hand-written rule is ever
   250	silently rewritten.
   251	
   252	### Category
   253	
   254	The groups, each with its colour, and a `+ add` button. Adding a group asks for a label and a
   255	colour; its stored name is derived from the label and never shown, which is why relabelling or
   256	recolouring later touches no entry. Adding one writes `groups.md` immediately rather than staging
   257	it: that is a different file from the entry, and a category must not disappear because the entry
   258	it was created for was discarded. A pen edits a group, a trashcan deletes it — and entries
   259	still naming a deleted group render grey.
   260	
   261	## Kanban
   262	
   263	Three columns — **todo** (red), **doing** (yellow), **done** (green) — holding one sprint's
   264	tasks. Every task is a card and every card is a task; events never appear.
   265	
   266	A sprint is a date range, not a stored field: sprint 1 starts on the *kanban first week start
   267	date* and each one runs for the *kanban interval*. A task's sprint is whichever range its start
   268	falls in, so the number can never disagree with the date, and moving a card to another sprint
   269	is exactly a change of its start and end. Both settings therefore live in the data repo, not on
   270	the device — if they differed between two devices the same card would be in different sprints.
   271	
   272	A repeating task contributes one card per occurrence inside the sprint. Moving one records an
   273	override for that occurrence alone; the rule itself is never rewritten.
   274	
   275	Each column header shows its state and a `+` that creates a task in that stage, on the first day
   276	of the selected sprint. **The state's name carries the colour** — `todo` red, `doing` yellow,
   277	`done` green, the board's own three colours exactly, the yellow being the cards' `#e0a500` rather
   278	than a pure one, which would not be readable on the light theme. There is no colour dot and no
   279	card count: the dot said what the coloured name now says, and a count is a number nobody acts
   280	on. The name is **centred and drawn at twice the size**; the `+` stays at the right of the
   281	header, where it is the board's only way to make a task, since the top pane has none. The sprint
   282	selector and a filter icon (category, assignee, priority) sit in the top pane, because one board
   283	shows one sprint.
   284	
   285	A card shows:
   286

   288	  `<` `>`** to move the card to the previous or next stage — `<` disabled in todo, `>` disabled
   289	  in done. **On a desktop it does not**: all three columns are there and the card is dragged
   290	  between them, so arrows on every card are a second way to do what the drag already does, in
   291	  the one place they are also easiest to mistake for the header's pager;
   292	- below it two lines of the markdown body;
   293	- on the right a priority chip (1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow), the estimate in days, and the sprint
   294	  number. Clicking any of the three changes it: the priority chip cycles 1 → 2 → 3, and the
   295	  estimate and the sprint ask for a number. Changing the sprint moves the task's start and end
   296	  into that sprint's range, keeping its offset within the sprint and its time of day.
   297	
   298	On desktop all three columns are shown and a card can be dragged between them, and each header is
   299	its stage's name, centred, with the `+` at its right and **no `‹` `›`** — with every column on
   300	screen there is nothing for a per-column pager to page. On a phone one column fills the screen
   301	and its header pages between the three: `[‹] doing [›]`, **centred as a group and drawn at twice
   302	the size**, the two buttons flanking the stage name on a background of their own — because the
   303	`<` `>` on a card mean something else entirely, they move that card. The group is sized so that
   304	it never exceeds the width of a 320 px screen. The header pair is disabled at todo and at done
   305	rather than wrapping.
   306	
   307	**There is no swipe on the board.** A sideways gesture on a column or a card does nothing. The
   308	only swipe in the calendar is on the period label in the top pane, which steps the sprint — so a
   309	gesture here never has to be told apart from a drag.
   310	
   311	**Exactly one column is visible at a time.** No part of the next column may show at the edge of
   312	the screen: a sliver of `done` beside `doing` is a layout fault, and the cause is always the
   313	same — a gap between columns in a strip that is shifted by whole column widths.
   314	
   315	Cards are not reordered by hand; their order comes from priority and start.
   316	
   317	## Settings
   318	
   319	The gear button opens a centred panel whose top right has an `x` to close:
   320	
   321	- **Groups** — the list of groups, each with its colour, a pen to edit and a `+` to add.
   322	- **Start week on** — Monday or Sunday.
   323	- **Time zone** — a zone name such as `Europe/Berlin`, defaulting to the device's own. This
   324	  zone, not the device's, decides which day a timed entry lands in, where it sits in the week and
   325	  day grids, and what a time you type means. A plain `UTC+1` is not offered: it is an hour wrong
   326	  for half the year in any zone with daylight saving. All-day entries are bare dates and are
   327	  never run through it at all.
   328	- **Date format** — `auto` (the device's locale), `dd.mm.yyyy` or `mm/dd/yy`.
   329	- **Show calendar weeks** — the month view's week-number gutter. The week view's label carries
   330	  its ISO week number either way.
   331	- **Kanban interval** — in weeks.
   332	- **Kanban first week start date**.
   333	- **Theme** — system, light or dark.
   334	
   335	Everything here is stored on the device except the groups, the kanban interval and the kanban
   336	first week start date, which are data and live in the repo so they follow you and mean the same
   337	thing everywhere. Theme and date format apply to all of Mine, not the calendar alone, and the
   338	main app's settings shows the same two rows.

   341	
   342	The views above describe the desktop. The same screens adapt:
   343	
   344	- The top pane holds five controls — `[board] [filter] [NOV/26 ▾] [⚙] [⌂]` — at twice their old
   345	  size, sharing the row width equally on **one line at every phone width**, 320 px included.

   348	- A month cell shows at most two entry lines, then `+N`; a line carries the title alone, with no
   349	  time prefix and no done-rectangle, clipped at the cell's edge. A year cell stays a coloured

   355	  and its cards keep their own `<` `>` because there is nothing to drag a card onto.
   356	
   357	**Every view fits a 320 CSS px viewport**, with the week gutter on and whatever the entries happen

   362	the screen has is a defect even when it looks right on a desktop, and a cell insisting on room

   366	
   367	## On the main screen
   368	
   369	The tile screen of the main app shows today's entries and the next one coming up.

   138	### The day preview
   139	
   140	Clicking a day opens that day's entries as a list, each one tappable. Its top right carries a
   141	small `+` to add an entry on that day and a small `x` to close it — not full-width buttons. It
   142	is reached from a day in the year grid, from a day cell in the month view on a phone, and from
   143	a day header in the week and day grids.
   144	
   145	## Entry popup
   146	
   147	The popup **opens in the middle of the screen**, on a phone as much as on a desktop — and so
   148	does every other overlay in the calendar: a field's own popup, the settings panel and the day
   149	preview. Nothing rises from the bottom edge any more. A centred card is reached with either
   150	thumb and does not pretend to be a drawer that can be dragged.
   151	
   152	A row of icon buttons at the top, and it now holds the type pair and the three on the right and
   153	nothing between them. **Every button in it is an icon; no button carries a letter.**
   154	
   155	- Leftmost, a ticked square for **task** and a calendar page for **event**. Choosing one
   156	  deselects the other; the default is event. What the entry *is* comes first, because it governs
   157	  what the rest of the popup offers.
   158	- Then, right-aligned: an `x` to close and discard, a trashcan to delete the entry, and a disk
   159	  to save it.
   160	
   161	There is no dash between the two groups: the gap to the right-aligned trio already separates
   162	them, and the field icons the dash used to divide off are not in this row at all any more.
   163	
   164	Below it, in this order: the **title**, the **start and end** fields, the **toggle row**, and
   165	then **one row per field**.
   166	
   167	### The toggle row
   168	
   169	One row of icons directly under start and end. These are not fields with a form each: they are
   170	small values, edited in the row itself, and they **show their value** rather than merely whether
   171	they have one — each as a small badge on the corner of its icon.
   172	
   173	- a sun for **all-day**. **A clickable icon, not a checkbox** — lit when on, plain when off, the
   174	  one icon in the popup that still lights, because it is the one with no value to show. On an
   175	  event it is alone on the row.
   176	- three small columns for **stage** — cycles `todo` → `doing` → `done` on each tap, its badge in
   177	  that stage's kanban colour: red, yellow, green. There is no stage popup.
   178	- a flag for **priority** — cycles none → 1 → 2 → 3 → none, the badge carrying the digit on that
   179	  priority's chip colour.
   180	- an hourglass for **estimate** — the one that opens a popup, because a number has to be typed.
   181	  Its badge reads the day count as `2d`, exactly as a kanban card shows it. It stays on this row
   182	  rather than joining the field rows below, because what it carries is a badge-sized value like
   183	  the other three, not a form.
   184	
   185	On an event, stage, priority and estimate are not there at all, because an event has none of
   186	them. They sit here so that a task that is not on a board still carries the two fields a kanban
   187	card edits.
   188	
   189	All-day is deliberately **not** the save button's green: in all of Mine green is a save and red
   190	is a trashcan, and a green toggle beside the disk would make the popup look like it offers two
   191	primary actions.
   192	
   193	### The field rows
   194	
   195	Every other field is a row, and **every field has a row, set or not** — the rows are now the only
   196	way to reach a field, so none of them can be hidden. A row is the icon on the left and the
   197	field's name beside it, and, when the field is set, its value after that:
   198	
   199	```
   200	[ball]    Category     Work
   201	[pin]     Location     Conference room 3B
   202	[lines]   Details
   203	[repeat]  Repeat
   204	```
   205	
   206	The six fields, in their canonical order:
   207	
   208	- three lines of text for **details** — the markdown body;
   209	- a ball for **category**;
   210	- circular arrows for **repetition**;
   211	- a bell for **alerts**;
   212	- a pin for **location**;
   213	- a person for **participants**.
   214	
   215	- **Clicking a row opens that field's popup.** The row *is* the pen, so no row carries one, and
   216	  clearing a field is the trashcan inside its popup, which is already there.
   217	- **The rows that are set move to the top.** Set fields come first, unset ones follow, and inside
   218	  each group the order is always the canonical one above. Setting a field lifts its row into the
   219	  top group and shuffles nothing else, so a row never moves for a reason you did not cause.
   220	- **A set row is plain.** Being in the top group and showing a value is what says the field is
   221	  set — which is what the old lit icon said, in a row that no longer exists. Nothing in the
   222	  popup lights except the sun.
   223	
   224	Each of the six opens its own popup, and every popup has the same three buttons: a trashcan that
   225	clears that one field, an `x` that abandons the sub-edit, and a disk that commits the value into
   226	the entry form. **A sub-popup never writes to the repo**, with the single exception noted under
   227	Category.
   228	Nothing is written until the entry popup's own disk, so one entry edit is one commit, and the
   229	entry popup's `x` discards the staged fields along with everything else. This is also what makes
   230	a brand-new entry work, since it has no file for a sub-popup to write to.
   231	
   232	Saving **closes the popup and returns to the calendar immediately**; the push to GitHub runs in
   233	the background and is reported in the sync line, not in the popup.
   234	
   235	### Repetition
   236	
   237	A dropdown, not an RRULE field:
   238	
   239	```
   240	does not repeat · daily · weekly · every 2 weeks ·
   241	monthly on the x-th · monthly on the x-th weekday · yearly
   242	```
   243	
   244	below it an **ends** control: never, on a date, or after a number of occurrences.
   245	
   246	Files may be hand-written or imported, so a rule the dropdown cannot express — `the last Friday
   247	of the month`, `Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays` — is shown as a non-selectable **custom** state
   248	displaying the rule as text, with a note that choosing an option will replace it. Saving the
   249	entry without touching the dropdown leaves the rule untouched. No hand-written rule is ever
   250	silently rewritten.
   251	
   252	### Category
   253	
   254	The groups, each with its colour, and a `+ add` button. Adding a group asks for a label and a
   255	colour; its stored name is derived from the label and never shown, which is why relabelling or
   256	recolouring later touches no entry. Adding one writes `groups.md` immediately rather than staging
   257	it: that is a different file from the entry, and a category must not disappear because the entry
   258	it was created for was discarded. A pen edits a group, a trashcan deletes it — and entries
   259	still naming a deleted group render grey.
   260	
   261	## Kanban
   262	
   263	Three columns — **todo** (red), **doing** (yellow), **done** (green) — holding one sprint's
   264	tasks. Every task is a card and every card is a task; events never appear.
   265	
   266	A sprint is a date range, not a stored field: sprint 1 starts on the *kanban first week start
   267	date* and each one runs for the *kanban interval*. A task's sprint is whichever range its start
   268	falls in, so the number can never disagree with the date, and moving a card to another sprint
   269	is exactly a change of its start and end. Both settings therefore live in the data repo, not on
   270	the device — if they differed between two devices the same card would be in different sprints.
   271	
   272	A repeating task contributes one card per occurrence inside the sprint. Moving one records an
   273	override for that occurrence alone; the rule itself is never rewritten.
   274	
   275	Each column header shows its state and a `+` that creates a task in that stage, on the first day
   276	of the selected sprint. **The state's name carries the colour** — `todo` red, `doing` yellow,
   277	`done` green, the board's own three colours exactly, the yellow being the cards' `#e0a500` rather
   278	than a pure one, which would not be readable on the light theme. There is no colour dot and no
   279	card count: the dot said what the coloured name now says, and a count is a number nobody acts
   280	on. The name is **centred and drawn at twice the size**; the `+` stays at the right of the
   281	header, where it is the board's only way to make a task, since the top pane has none. The sprint
   282	selector and a filter icon (category, assignee, priority) sit in the top pane, because one board
   283	shows one sprint.
   284	
   285	A card shows:
   286	
   287	- a top row with a trashcan to delete, a pen to edit, and the title. **On a phone it also carries
   288	  `<` `>`** to move the card to the previous or next stage — `<` disabled in todo, `>` disabled
   289	  in done. **On a desktop it does not**: all three columns are there and the card is dragged
   290	  between them, so arrows on every card are a second way to do what the drag already does, in
   291	  the one place they are also easiest to mistake for the header's pager;
   292	- below it two lines of the markdown body;
   293	- on the right a priority chip (1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow), the estimate in days, and the sprint
   294	  number. Clicking any of the three changes it: the priority chip cycles 1 → 2 → 3, and the
   295	  estimate and the sprint ask for a number. Changing the sprint moves the task's start and end
   296	  into that sprint's range, keeping its offset within the sprint and its time of day.
   297	
   298	On desktop all three columns are shown and a card can be dragged between them, and each header is
   299	its stage's name, centred, with the `+` at its right and **no `‹` `›`** — with every column on
   300	screen there is nothing for a per-column pager to page. On a phone one column fills the screen
   301	and its header pages between the three: `[‹] doing [›]`, **centred as a group and drawn at twice
   302	the size**, the two buttons flanking the stage name on a background of their own — because the
   303	`<` `>` on a card mean something else entirely, they move that card. The group is sized so that
   304	it never exceeds the width of a 320 px screen. The header pair is disabled at todo and at done
   305	rather than wrapping.
   306	
   307	**There is no swipe on the board.** A sideways gesture on a column or a card does nothing. The
   308	only swipe in the calendar is on the period label in the top pane, which steps the sprint — so a
   309	gesture here never has to be told apart from a drag.
   310	
   311	**Exactly one column is visible at a time.** No part of the next column may show at the edge of
   312	the screen: a sliver of `done` beside `doing` is a layout fault, and the cause is always the
   313	same — a gap between columns in a strip that is shifted by whole column widths.
   314	
   315	Cards are not reordered by hand; their order comes from priority and start.
   316	
   317	## Settings
   318	
   319	The gear button opens a centred panel whose top right has an `x` to close:
   320	
   321	- **Groups** — the list of groups, each with its colour, a pen to edit and a `+` to add.
   322	- **Start week on** — Monday or Sunday.
   323	- **Time zone** — a zone name such as `Europe/Berlin`, defaulting to the device's own. This
   324	  zone, not the device's, decides which day a timed entry lands in, where it sits in the week and
   325	  day grids, and what a time you type means. A plain `UTC+1` is not offered: it is an hour wrong
   326	  for half the year in any zone with daylight saving. All-day entries are bare dates and are
   327	  never run through it at all.
   328	- **Date format** — `auto` (the device's locale), `dd.mm.yyyy` or `mm/dd/yy`.
   329	- **Show calendar weeks** — the month view's week-number gutter. The week view's label carries
   330	  its ISO week number either way.
   331	- **Kanban interval** — in weeks.
   332	- **Kanban first week start date**.
   333	- **Theme** — system, light or dark.
   334	
   335	Everything here is stored on the device except the groups, the kanban interval and the kanban
   336	first week start date, which are data and live in the repo so they follow you and mean the same
   337	thing everywhere. Theme and date format apply to all of Mine, not the calendar alone, and the
   338	main app's settings shows the same two rows.
   339	
   340	## On a phone
   341	
   342	The views above describe the desktop. The same screens adapt:
   343	
   344	- The top pane holds five controls — `[board] [filter] [NOV/26 ▾] [⚙] [⌂]` — at twice their old
   345	  size, sharing the row width equally on **one line at every phone width**, 320 px included.
   346	  There are no `‹` `›`: the label is swiped left and right instead, and the caret `▾` on it still
   347	  opens the picker.
   348	- A month cell shows at most two entry lines, then `+N`; a line carries the title alone, with no
   349	  time prefix and no done-rectangle, clipped at the cell's edge. A year cell stays a coloured
   350	  day.
   351	- Tapping a day in the month or year view opens that day's entries as a centred card, each one
   352	  tappable, with the small `+` and `x` in its top right — so nothing is ever smaller than a
   353	  finger. Tapping a month's name in the year view zooms into that month instead.
   354	- The kanban shows one column at a time, paged by the centred, double-size `‹` `›` in its header,
   355	  and its cards keep their own `<` `>` because there is nothing to drag a card onto.
   356	
   357	**Every view fits a 320 CSS px viewport**, with the week gutter on and whatever the entries happen
   358	to be — the double-size top pane and the double-size kanban header included. **Nothing in the app
   359	moves sideways**: no view scrolls or extends horizontally, in any view, at any width. The period
   360	label's swipe is no exception, because it moves the period, not the layout. A view that demands
   361	more width than
   362	the screen has is a defect even when it looks right on a desktop, and a cell insisting on room
   363	for a time, a title and an icon at once is the usual cause — seven of them across a phone is
   364	where it shows. `test/run.sh` checks every view at 320 and 360 px, in light and dark; see
   365	[../TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md](../TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md).
   366	
   367	## On the main screen
   368	
   369	The tile screen of the main app shows today's entries and the next one coming up.

content.text:
I've read `REQUIREMENTS.md` (369 lines), `TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md`, `TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md` and the implementation. Here's what I found before I start asking.

**One of your items is a plain bug, not a requirements conflict:** in `calendar/views.js:280` the `#view` click delegation opens `[data-key]` on *any* click inside a card, so the chips' and arrows' own handlers fire and then the event bubbles up and opens the ticket too. Confirmed cause, no ambiguity.

**The rest contradict REQUIREMENTS.md in 11 places.** Notable ones:
- Priority 1/2/3 is load-bearing: `REQUIREMENTS.md:13` (entry fields), `:178` (flag cycles 1→2→3), `:295` (chip 1 red/2 orange/3 yellow), `:316` (card order comes from priority), the kanban filter's P1/P2/P3 chips, plus `TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md:43` mapping it to RFC 5545 `PRIORITY` 1-9 and a sample file carrying `priority: 2`.
- The day view's `TUE 20` header is also the **click target that opens the day preview** (`REQUIREMENTS.md:142`, `views.js:288`). Removing it removes that path.
- Moving the `x` rightmost evicts the disk from the rightmost corner, which the root `REQUIREMENTS.md` justifies explicitly ("the familiar icon in the familiar corner").
- The card's sprint chip is the only way to move a task to another sprint (`REQUIREMENTS.md:296`).
- The filter's group list is multi-select (hide any subset); a dropdown is normally single-select.

Let me work through these.

| Key | Applies to | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | both | required |
| `type` | both | `event` or `task` |
| `start` | both | `DTSTART`. A bare date (`2026-04-18`) is all-day; a timestamp (`2026-04-18T14:00:00Z`) is an instant |
| `end` | both | same value types as `start`; omitted when a single all-day item |
| `group` | both | a name, resolved through `groups.md` |
| `stage` | `task` only | `todo` / `doing` / `done`. Replaces the old `done` boolean |
| `priority` | `task` only | `PRIORITY`, 1-9. The UI writes 1-3, and those three read back unchanged; a hand-written 4-6 reads as 2 and 7-9 as 3 |
| `estimate` | `task` only | days. Ours, no RFC 5545 equivalent |
| `location` | both | free text |
| `alerts` | both | minutes before start, `0` = at start. Stored and exported only; nothing fires in the background |
| `participants` | both | list of email addresses |
| `recurrence` | both | RRULE string, e.g. `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SA` |
| `exdate` / `rdate` | recurring | occurrences to skip / extra occurrences |
| `status` | override | `cancelled` removes the occurrence. The only value used |
| `series` | override | id of the recurring file it belongs to |
| `recurrence-id` | override | the original occurrence date this file replaces |
| `conflictOf` | conflict file | written by sync |

No `duration` key — it is `end - start`.

Type and time are independent: `type` decides whether the entry has a stage, a priority and an
estimate, the value type of `start` decides whether it is all-day or timed. A task is usually
all-day, but may carry a time and then renders at it.

**The entry popup's icon row, toggle row and field rows.** That the icon row holds icons alone,
with no letter anywhere in it, and that it holds nothing but the type pair and the three on the
right — task, event, then close, delete, save — with no field icon and no dash left in it.

That a new entry is an event and its toggle row holds the sun by itself; that choosing a task
puts stage, priority and estimate on that same row and switching back to an event takes all
three away again. That stage cycles through three stages in three badge colours and back, that
priority cycles 1, 2, 3, none with the digit on its own colour, and that the estimate opens a
popup prefilled with one day, badges `3d` once set and loses its badge once cleared. That all-day
lights with the ordinary enabled background and never with `--good`, because green is the save
button's. That the row sits **below** the start and end fields, not above them — resolved from
the elements' document order, since a row that merely looks right can still be the old one.

That the six field rows read details, category, repeat, alerts, location, participants, in that
order on a task and on an event alike, each one carrying its icon and its name; that every field
has a row whether it is set or not; that setting one moves its row above the unset ones while the
order inside each group stays canonical; that a set row shows the field's value and no pen; and
that a set row carries no enabled background, because position and value are what say it is set.

**The popup is centred.** At 320 px, that the entry popup, a field sub-popup, the settings panel
and the day preview each sit clear of the bottom edge — their bounding box's bottom is above the
viewport's, and their top below it. Nothing in the app is a bottom sheet any more, and a card
that still stretches to the bottom edge is the old sheet in new paint.

zoom buttons are gone, and a check for their absence is what keeps them gone. That **clicking the
label walks the zoom** year → month → week → day → year, round the cycle, with nothing disabled
at an end. That on the board clicking the label opens the sprint list instead and does not zoom.
That the **caret is a button of its own** and opens the picker, and that clicking the label does
not open it. That the board icon reaches the kanban and is a calendar icon there, returning to

its ISO number with *show calendar weeks* off.

period group, then settings and home — read from their left edges, so a reordering that looks
right but wires the wrong button cannot pass. That at 320 px the pane is **one line**: every
control's bounding box shares the same row, none wraps to a second, and none is dropped. That
the `‹` `›` are not rendered at that width, and that a horizontal swipe on the label steps the

text colour and its background must be transparent. A filled green button anywhere in Mine is a
failure, so the check reads the background as well as the colour — that is the half of it that
can catch a regression to the old style.

**What a saved task writes.** A new task saved with nothing but a title must land as
`stage: todo` with `estimate: 1`, and a task whose estimate was cleared must have no `estimate`
key at all — not an empty one, and never `None`. This is the check that holds the file format
to [calendar/TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](calendar/TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md), and it reads the
file back out of the local mirror rather than trusting the form.

## A check must be able to fail

Before trusting a new check, break the thing it covers and watch it go red. A fit check written
against `--window-size` passes on a broken layout; a colour check that names `#0a7b3e` instead
of resolving `--good` passes when the token changes underneath it. Removing `min-width: 0` from
`.day` must turn the month fit checks red, and putting it back must turn them green.

## What the harness cannot tell you

Headless Chromium on a desktop is not a phone. It does not cover:

- **the real device** — a system font scale, a notch, a software keyboard, Safari's and
  Chrome's own quirks. Serve the tree with `python3 -m http.server` and open it from the phone
  on the same network, or push and open the live URL.
- **installing to the home screen, the service worker and the update banner** — these need an
  installed app over HTTPS. `spike/` covers the platform questions and needs no token.

text colour and its background must be transparent. A filled green button anywhere in Mine is a
failure, so the check reads the background as well as the colour — that is the half of it that
can catch a regression to the old style.

**What a saved task writes.** A new task saved with nothing but a title must land as
`stage: todo` with `estimate: 1`, and a task whose estimate was cleared must have no `estimate`
key at all — not an empty one, and never `None`. This is the check that holds the file format
to [calendar/TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](calendar/TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md), and it reads the
file back out of the local mirror rather than trusting the form.

## A check must be able to fail

Before trusting a new check, break the thing it covers and watch it go red. A fit check written
against `--window-size` passes on a broken layout; a colour check that names `#0a7b3e` instead
of resolving `--good` passes when the token changes underneath it. Removing `min-width: 0` from
`.day` must turn the month fit checks red, and putting it back must turn them green.

## What the harness cannot tell you

Headless Chromium on a desktop is not a phone. It does not cover:

- **the real device** — a system font scale, a notch, a software keyboard, Safari's and
  Chrome's own quirks. Serve the tree with `python3 -m http.server` and open it from the phone
  on the same network, or push and open the live URL.
- **installing to the home screen, the service worker and the update banner** — these need an
  installed app over HTTPS. `spike/` covers the platform questions and needs no token.

every entry, and there is no cap on the number of groups. Unknown group renders grey. It lives in
the data repo, so the mapping follows you across devices.

## Settings

Two of the settings are data, not preferences, and live in `calendar/settings.md`:

```yaml
---
kanban-anchor: 2026-01-05     # bare date: the first day of sprint 1
kanban-interval: 2            # weeks
---
```

With no `settings.md` at all the anchor is `2024-01-01`, a Monday, and the interval is 2 weeks.
That fallback is a constant rather than anything read off the device, so two devices still agree
on the numbering before the file exists.

They are in the repo because the sprint a task belongs to is *derived* from them. On the device
they would make the same file report a different sprint on a phone than on a laptop, and moving
a card would then write the wrong date. Everything else — theme, date format, time zone, week
start, show-calendar-weeks, the group filter — is a device preference in IndexedDB, the group
filter under `calendar.hiddenGroups` as it already is. Theme and date format are Mine-wide keys,
not the calendar's.

## Sprints

There is no `sprint` key. Sprint *n* runs from `anchor + (n-1) × interval` weeks for `interval`
weeks, and a task's sprint is whichever range its `start` falls in. So:

- the number can never contradict the date, because there is only the date;
- moving a card to another sprint is a write of `start` and `end` and nothing else;
- changing the interval renumbers every card at once, which is correct — it is one timeline.

Computed on bare dates in whole days, never through a `Date` at local midnight: the anchor is a
bare date and sprint boundaries must not shift by a day with the viewer's zone. A `start` before
the anchor has no sprint and the card is not on the board.

## Time zone

One IANA zone name, defaulting to `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`, decides

kanban-interval: 2

A `start` before the anchor has no sprint, and such a task is not on the board.

The four spec files are updated. Nothing in `calendar/*.js` or `test/check.mjs` was touched — these are requirements only, so the code still implements the old behaviour.

## What each answer became

**Important replaces priority** — `calendar/REQUIREMENTS.md` now states it as a yes/no with its reasoning, `important: true` written only when true, and `priority: 1` reading as important while `2`–`9` read as not. `calendar/TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md:43` swaps the `PRIORITY` row for `important` and adds a paragraph calling `priority` the one key in the format that is read but never written.

**`24h`** replaces the sun as a lit toggle; the all-day strip in the grids and the prose keep the word "all-day", stated explicitly so nobody "fixes" the inconsistency later.

**`!`** is a lit toggle in the popup and a plain, unpressable marker before the card's title. Cards sort important-first, then by start.

**The `x` is rightmost** — documented in `calendar/REQUIREMENTS.md` for the entry popup and the six sub-popups, and the root `REQUIREMENTS.md` gained a second convention paragraph, since its "familiar corner" argument had been the reason the disk sat there.

**The day view loses its header row**; the week view keeps its seven, and the day-preview entry points now read "year grid, phone month cell, week-view day header."

**Settings** is an eight-row two-column grid, labels shortened to `Sprint length` and `First sprint` — with a note that the repo keys stay `kanban-interval` and `kanban-anchor` — groups behind an *edit groups* button opening the category popup in manage-only form, and no closing paragraph.

**Kanban cards** hold a title, an optional `!`, two body lines and the day. No pen, trashcan, estimate, sprint or chip. Deletion is the popup's trashcan plus its skip control. Sprint moves are date edits, and `REQUIREMENTS.md:296` is gone.

**The icon-click bug** is written in as a rule — "clicking a card opens it; clicking a control on a card does not" — and `TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md` asks for a check that goes red when a handler stops at the button but lets the event bubble.

**The filter** folds the group checkboxes into a `groups` dropdown with multi-select intact, and the board's four priority chips become one *important only* toggle.

## Two things to flag

- **`test/check.mjs` has assertions that will now fail by design** — line 253 checks `priority cycles 1, 2, 3, none`, and line 214's row check still passes but the desktop-card assertion expecting a trashcan and a pen does not. They need rewriting alongside the implementation.
- **Three tiers collapsing to one is lossy in your existing data**: you chose that `priority: 2` and `3` read as not important, so any task currently marked P2 or P3 silently loses its marker on first read. `calendar/sample/2026/04/2026-04-20-0000-t2wv.md` carries `priority: 2` and three lines of prose about the key — I left the sample files alone since you scoped the update to the three spec files. Say the word and I'll bring the sample in line too.

     2	# Starts the fixture server and a headless Chromium, runs the browser checks, tears both down.

     8	set -u
     9	HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
    10	PORT=8787
    11	PROFILE=$(mktemp -d)
    12	
    13	cleanup() {
    14	  [ -n "${CHROME:-}" ] && kill "$CHROME" 2>/dev/null
    15	  [ -n "${SERVER:-}" ] && kill "$SERVER" 2>/dev/null
    16	  rm -rf "$PROFILE"
    17	}
    18	trap cleanup EXIT
    19	
    20	command -v chromium >/dev/null || { echo "chromium not on PATH"; exit 2; }
    21	
    22	python3 "$HERE/serve.py" $PORT >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    23	SERVER=$!
    24	chromium --headless --no-sandbox --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --no-first-run \
    25	  --disable-extensions --remote-debugging-port=9222 --user-data-dir="$PROFILE" \
    26	  about:blank >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    27	CHROME=$!
    28	
    29	for i in $(seq 30); do

    31	  sleep 0.2
    32	done
    33	
    34	# Node 20 keeps WebSocket behind a flag; 21+ ignores the flag harmlessly.
    35	node --experimental-websocket "$HERE/check.mjs" "$@" 2>&1 | grep -v 'ExperimentalWarning\|Use `node'
    36	exit "${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
